Modal Harmony #1.heading: Hear the bass and triad. Find their modal colour.
Modal Harmony #1.intro: You will hear one bass note with a major three-note chord above it. Choose the full label that matches the combined sound.

steps.title: Listen to the combined sound
steps.description: Press Play to hear the bass note and the three higher notes together. Listen for the lower note underneath the chord. You can listen again whenever you need to.

steps.title: Choose the matching label
steps.description: Each answer gives a modal name and the upper chord’s relationship to the bass. Choose the whole label, not just the modal name. The bass is always C in this lesson.

steps.title: Submit your answer
steps.description: When you are ready, press Submit Answer. You can change your choice before you submit.

Modal Harmony #1.about: A triad is a chord made of three notes. In this quiz, a single bass note sits below a major triad. The modal names label the colours taught for these bass-and-chord combinations. The Roman numerals describe where the upper chord is built relative to the bass. For example, II means the second note and V means the fifth. With C as the bass, those notes are D and G. A ♭ before a numeral lowers that note by one keyboard step, counting both white and black keys. This lesson keeps C as the bass throughout. Each combination has two arrangements of the upper notes. Choose the same label for either arrangement; there is no separate inversion answer.
Modal Harmony #1.exampleExplanation: D major is built on D, the second note above C in the C major scale. The full answer is Lydian Dominant · II Major. The bass C and all three upper notes sound at the same time. This is a visual example.
